accepted_phrases: The frozen caffeine reference gives serving-level examples, states that arabica typically contains about half the caffeine of robusta, and says dark-roast coffee generally has very slightly less caffeine than lighter roast because roasting reduces caffeine content. This rebuts the beginner shortcut that a dark label itself means a larger caffeine dose, but it does not determine the exact caffeine in any captured bag or cup. The illy listing identifies a dark-roast 100 percent arabica ground moka product, while the DOTA listing identifies a light-roast ground arabica product and offers roast variants. Neither listing provides a standardized dose, measured caffeine, grind mass, water ratio, extraction yield, or brewed serving result. A cup comparison therefore requires bean species, dose or mass, grind, method, water ratio, serving size, and an actual caffeine measurement rather than roast color alone.

The storage reference distinguishes roasted whole beans from grounds, recommends airtight light-protected storage for whole beans, and says increased surface area causes grounds to go stale in days rather than weeks. The preparation reference says roasted beans must be ground before brewing, identifies grind size, water temperature, brew time, and coffee-to-water ratio as extraction variables, and notes that whole or ground coffee is often vacuum packed to limit oxidation. The burr-mill reference explains adjustable coarse-to-fine grinding and that grind ranges differ across espresso, pour-over, drip, French press, and other methods. These sources justify treating whole-bean freshness and method-matched grinding as a system decision, not as proof that every whole-bean bag stays fresh for a fixed number of weeks. The Java Planet listing offers a whole-bean sampler but no grinder, brewer, roast date, opened-package storage outcome, or total-system cost, so it cannot by itself support the whole-bean route for this beginner.

The DOTA light-roast ground listing displays $15.99, 87 percent of 100 from twelve reviews, and SKU B08MBKJGCP; the Java Planet whole-bean sampler displays $34.99 with no reviews and SKU B01MSNNM5X. These are frozen offer facts and seller descriptions, not sensory tests or longitudinal beginner outcomes. A French-press discussion contains one author's enthusiasm, cleanup concerns, a report of plunger threading failing after about two months, and a comment that pour-over can require fresh beans and a good grinder; it is useful for identifying maintenance, fragility, and grinder-cost questions but is not a controlled comparison of the captured products. The two short grinder posts are especially limited: one reports eleven years of daily use without naming a verifiable model in the frozen body, and the other reports daily use of a Braun coffee or spice grinder since 1992. They are distractor anecdotes and cannot support a new grinder model, a grinder category lifetime, or a purchase recommendation.

The frozen moka reference says a moka pot uses vapor pressure and heat-driven gas expansion to pass hot water through ground coffee. It also states that typical moka extraction uses about one to two bar while espresso standards specify nine bar, so moka coffee is not considered espresso. The captured Puerto Rican bundle listing displays $34.99, 73 percent of 100 from three reviews, SKU B09PHVT7FF, a six-cup aluminum stovetop maker, and a four-ounce ground-coffee sample; it calls the device a stovetop espresso maker and says steam pressure drives water through grounds. The illy listing displays $12.10, 80 percent of 100 from twelve reviews, SKU B08QG21HWB, and says its ground moka coffee is finely ground for a stovetop moka pot. Together these establish a captured compatible product category and a possible low-commitment trial, but they do not independently establish cafe quality, nine-bar espresso, actual cup output, stove compatibility, safety, cleanup burden, durability, or beginner retention.

Before choosing a path, verify the exact moka maker's stove and material compatibility, nominal versus actual beverage output, serving fit, valve and gasket condition, grind requirement, cleaning and stopping procedure, current seller, return path, and whether the stated sample is included. For any separate pre-ground path, identify the exact compatible brewer and total cost. For the whole-bean path, identify a method-matched grinder, adjustment range, current cost, cleaning and retention burden, warranty, and brewer. Record roast or pack date and storage plan rather than assuming a universal freshness deadline. Use a small quantity and a returnable or already-owned brewer for the first repeated-use trial, track preparation time, cleanup, taste and whether the routine is actually sustained, and only then add a grinder or premium beans.

The frozen evidence does not support a unique best coffee or durable equipment winner. The whole-bean sampler plus new grinder is not an admissible immediate recommendation because no exact coffee grinder or complete system cost is captured, and the pre-ground plus separate-brewer path is incomplete because no exact compatible separate brewer is frozen. If the beginner verifies stove and material compatibility, serving output, safety and cleanup, current seller and return terms, the captured moka bundle is the only frozen offer that combines a brewer with a ground-coffee sample and is admissible as a narrow, reversible trial for strong moka coffee. It must not be sold as machine espresso or as proven cafe quality, and the separate illy bag should not be added until the included sample and routine have been tried. If those checks fail or the user does not want moka-style coffee, defer the exact purchase and first verify a complete method-specific system. A grinder, premium whole beans, or larger recurring coffee purchase becomes admissible only after the beginner demonstrates repeated use and supplies the missing exact-product, total-cost, and method-fit evidence.
After the exact moka maker passes stove, material, serving-output, safety, cleanup, seller, sample-inclusion, and return checks, use the captured bundle only as a small returnable moka-coffee trial.
Conditionally trial the six-cup moka bundle with its included ground sample after every compatibility and returnability check passes, without calling it machine espresso.
Defer an exact purchase while stove compatibility, serving fit, cleanup tolerance, seller and return terms, dates, method fit, or complete-system cost remains unresolved.
Choose explicit deferral unless the moka preflight passes or another complete method-specific brewer, grinder if needed, and total cost are verified.

The beginner wants strong moka-style coffee and verifies the exact maker's stove and material compatibility, serving output, valve and gasket condition, safe procedure, cleanup fit, included sample, current seller, and usable return path.
The trial produces moka coffee and must not be described as nine-bar machine espresso or proven cafe quality.
Use the included four-ounce ground sample before adding the separate illy bag or a larger recurring coffee purchase.
A returnable trial tests routine fit but the listing ratings and marketing do not prove durability, taste preference, or long-term retention.

The beginner does not want moka-style coffee, a moka compatibility or safety check fails, or the exact brewer, grinder if required, seller, return path, date, serving fit, and complete-system cost remain unresolved.
The frozen sources do not establish a unique best coffee or durable equipment winner.
A pre-ground bag alone is not a complete route because an exact compatible brewer and its total cost are still required.
The whole-bean sampler route remains deferred until a method-matched grinder, brewer, adjustment needs, cleaning burden, warranty, and complete-system cost are supplied.
The illy dark-roast label proves that every brewed serving contains more caffeine than the captured DOTA light-roast coffee.
Every unopened or opened whole-bean and ground coffee product stays fresh for the same fixed number of weeks regardless of package and storage.
Because the listing calls the stovetop maker an espresso maker, the captured moka bundle produces the same nine-bar machine espresso as a cafe machine.
Frozen price, rating, review count, organic wording, and seller marketing independently prove taste quality, durability, beginner preference, and long-term retention.
The French-press discussion and the two short grinder posts are controlled tests of the captured products and prove a grinder model or category will last for decades.
The Java Planet sampler alone supplies a complete whole-bean brewing system with a suitable grinder, brewer, roast date, storage outcome, and verified total cost.
Buying either captured pre-ground bag is a complete brewed-coffee path even though no exact separate compatible brewer or total cost has been verified.
A unique best coffee and durable equipment winner can be selected before stove compatibility, serving output, safety, cleanup, seller, returns, dates, method fit, and complete-system cost are known.

research_subgoals.description: Build the frozen product matrix for the two ground coffees, the whole-bean sampler, and the moka bundle, preserving exact offer facts and identifying which brewer, grinder, date, and total-system fields are missing.
Determine what roast, bean species, and preparation evidence permits about caffeine and why roast color cannot determine the captured products' caffeine per cup.
Distinguish whole-bean and ground-coffee storage, method-matched grind, extraction variables, packaging, and total equipment commitment before evaluating the whole-bean route.
Reconcile moka method evidence with the moka-bundle and ground-moka listings, preserving the one-to-two-bar versus nine-bar boundary and every unresolved compatibility and use variable.

Use the preparation, storage, grinder, product, and community evidence to define a complete small, staged, reversible preflight for each route without transferring owner anecdotes beyond their context.

Select only a conditionally admissible moka trial or explicit deferral, reject incomplete pre-ground and whole-bean routes as immediate winners, and state why no unique coffee or durable equipment winner is supported.

query_requirements.text: Build a complete frozen product matrix for the two pre-ground bags, whole-bean sampler, and moka bundle, and separate displayed price, rating, review, SKU, contents, roast, bean, and grind facts from seller claims and missing system components.

Assess the dark-versus-light caffeine shortcut using bean species, roast, dose, grind, method, water ratio, serving size, and measurement boundaries without inventing caffeine values for either product.

Explain whole-bean versus ground-coffee storage and staling scope, method-matched grind and extraction variables, packaging limits, and the missing grinder, brewer, dates, and complete-system cost for the whole-bean route.

Compare the captured moka bundle and ground-moka coffee with the method evidence, distinguish moka pressure from nine-bar espresso, and identify serving, stove, material, safety, cleanup, seller, return, and durability gaps.

Scope the French-press and short grinder reports as anecdotes, then give a complete route-by-route preflight and a small repeated-use trial that tracks preparation, cleanup, taste, retention, seller, return, safety, dates, and total cost.

Choose among all four named candidate actions, state the conditions and tradeoffs for any admissible route, explicitly say whether a unique product winner is supported, and defer when the exact method fit or complete-system evidence is missing.
